title: Trial Registration, Pre-registration and Open Science

hook.en: Imagine a runner who decides which race to enter after seeing the results. That is what happens when a study picks its main outcome after looking at the data. Registration is the public record of "this is what we said we would do, before we knew the results". It keeps research honest.
hook.ur: Sochein ek daurne wala jo nateeje dekhne ke baad tay karta hai ke kaun si daur mein hissa liya. Yehi hota hai jab study data dekhne ke baad apna asal nateeja chunti hai. Registration is baat ka aam record hai ke "hum ne nateeje jaanne se pehle kaha tha hum kya karenge". Yeh research ko imaandar rakhta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain why trials and many other studies should be registered, register a protocol on a public registry, describe pre-registration and registered reports, and share data and materials openly in a responsible way.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke trials aur bohat si doosri studies register kyun hone chahiyen, public registry par protocol register karenge, pre-registration aur registered reports bayan karenge, aur data aur materials zimmedari se khulle taur par share karenge.

text.en: **Trial registration** means entering the key details of a study, such as the question, design, primary outcome and sample size, in a public registry **before the first participant is recruited**. Journals following the ICMJE rules will not publish trials that were not registered in advance. **Pre-registration** extends the idea to other studies, with a time-stamped plan that separates **confirmatory** analyses (planned) from **exploratory** ones. In **registered reports**, journals review the plan before results and agree to publish regardless of the outcome. **Open science** also means sharing data, code and materials where ethical.
text.ur: **Trial registration** ka matlab hai study ki bunyadi tafseelat, jaise sawal, design, primary outcome aur sample size, **pehle shirkat karne wale ki bharti se pehle** public registry mein darj karna. ICMJE ke qaide follow karne wale journals un trials ko shaya nahi karte jo pehle se register na hue hon. **Pre-registration** is khayal ko doosri studies tak barhata hai, waqt ki muhar lagi plan ke saath jo **tasdeeqi** (plan shuda) analyses ko **tajrabaati** analyses se alag karta hai. **Registered reports** mein journals nateeje se pehle plan ka jaiza lete hain aur nateeje se qata-e-nazar shaya karne par razi hote hain. **Open science** ka matlab data, code aur materials ko, jahan akhlaqi ho, share karna bhi hai.

text.en: Think of **a sealed prediction before a cricket match**. If you write "Pakistan will win by 20 runs" and seal it before the toss, everyone can check later whether you were right. If you write it after the match, it is worthless. Registration is the sealed envelope for research.
text.ur: **Cricket match se pehle band lifafe mein peshgoi** sochein. Agar aap toss se pehle likh kar band kar dein "Pakistan 20 runs se jeetega" to baad mein sab dekh sakte hain ke aap sahi thay ya nahi. Agar match ke baad likhein to bekaar hai. Registration research ka band lifafa hai.

question.en: A trial was registered with "pain at 6 weeks" as the primary outcome, but the published paper reports "function at 12 weeks" as the main result. What is this called?
question.ur: Ek trial "6 haftay par dard" primary outcome ke saath register hua, lekin shaya paper "12 haftay par function" ko asal nateeja batata hai. Isay kya kehte hain?

text.en: A normal part of peer review

feedback.en: Changing outcomes after seeing results biases findings.
feedback.ur: Nateeje dekhne ke baad outcomes badalna findings ko biased karta hai.

text.en: Outcome switching, which can hide a negative primary result and should be explained
text.ur: Outcome switching, jo manfi primary nateeja chhupa sakta hai aur jis ki wazahat honi chahiye

feedback.en: Yes — comparing the paper with the registration reveals it.
feedback.ur: Haan — paper ko registration se milane par pata chalta hai.

question.en: When should a trial be registered?

feedback.en: By then it is too late.
feedback.ur: Tab tak der ho chuki hoti hai.

text.en: Before the first participant is recruited
text.ur: Pehle shirkat karne wale ki bharti se pehle

feedback.en: Yes — that is the ICMJE requirement.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh ICMJE ka taqaza hai.

question.en: In a registered report, when does the journal decide whether to publish?
question.ur: Registered report mein journal kab tay karta hai ke shaya karna hai ya nahi?

text.en: Only after seeing whether the results are significant
text.ur: Sirf yeh dekh kar ke nateeje significant hain

feedback.en: That is the problem registered reports avoid.
feedback.ur: Registered reports isi masle se bachati hain.

text.en: After reviewing the plan (before results), and agreeing to publish whatever the outcome if the study follows the plan
text.ur: Plan ka jaiza lene ke baad (nateeje se pehle), aur agar study plan par chale to nateeje se qata-e-nazar shaya karne par razi

feedback.ur: Haan — yeh publication bias kam karta hai.

text.en: **Registering late or vaguely.** Registration after recruitment or with vague outcomes ("pain and function") does not protect against outcome switching. Be specific: which measure, what time point, which analysis. Update the registry if you change the plan, and explain the change in the paper. Another trap is thinking pre-registration forbids exploration; it does not, it asks you to label it as exploratory.
text.ur: **Der se ya mubham register karna.** Bharti ke baad ya mubham nateejon ("dard aur function") ke saath registration outcome switching se nahi bachata. Khaas hon: kaun sa naap, kaun sa waqt, kaun sa tajziya. Agar plan badlein to registry update karein, aur paper mein tabdeeli ki wazahat karein. Ek aur jaal yeh sochna hai ke pre-registration tajruba mana karti hai; aisa nahi, yeh kehti hai usay tajrabaati likhein.

text.en: **Check before you believe.** When you read a trial, search for its registration (usually the number is in the abstract). Compare the registered primary outcome with what was reported. If they differ, ask why. When you do your own study, register it for free and say so in your thesis, because it shows you are serious.
text.ur: **Yaqeen se pehle jaanchein.** Trial parhte waqt uski registration dhoondhein (aam taur par number abstract mein hota hai). Register shuda primary outcome ko report shuda se milayein. Agar mukhtalif ho to poochhein kyun. Apna study karte waqt isay muft register karein aur thesis mein batayein, kyunke yeh dikhata hai ke aap seriyas hain.

question.en: Why was trial registration introduced in the first place?
question.ur: Trial registration pehli baar kyun shuru hui?

answer.en: Because researchers found that trials with positive results were far more likely to be published than those with negative ones, and that the picture of treatments in journals was too rosy. Registration makes unpublished trials visible, so reviewers can find them. It was strengthened after cases in which harmful or ineffective treatments looked good because negative trials stayed hidden.
answer.ur: Kyunke muhaqqiqon ne paya ke musbat nateeje wale trials manfi walon se kahin zyada shaya hote hain, aur journals mein ilajon ki tasveer bohat gulabi thi. Registration ghair-shaya trials ko nazar aane wala banati hai, taake reviewers unhein dhoondh saken. Isay un cases ke baad mazboot kiya gaya jin mein nuqsandeh ya be-asar ilaaj is liye achhe lage ke manfi trials chhupe rahe.

beats.patient: A student plans a pilot trial of a home-based balance programme. Before recruiting, she registers it on a public registry with the primary outcome "Timed Up and Go at 8 weeks", the sample size and a short analysis plan.
beats.assessment: She also writes down that secondary outcomes such as fear of falling will be reported but are exploratory.
beats.treatment: After the trial, she reports all outcomes and notes where the analysis deviated from the plan, giving reasons.
beats.reassess: Her thesis and paper are trusted because the plan was public before the results.

text.en: **Registration includes safety.** State how adverse events will be monitored and reported. Open data must still protect participants: remove names and identifiers, share only what consent allows and use controlled-access repositories for sensitive data. Open does not mean careless.
text.ur: **Registration mein safety shamil hai.** Batayein adverse events ki nigrani aur report kaise hogi. Khula data bhi shirkat karne walon ko mehfooz rakhe: naam aur pehchanein hatayein, sirf wahi share karein jo razamandi ijazat de aur hassas data ke liye controlled-access repositories istemal karein. Khula hone ka matlab laparwai nahi.

text.en: In 2004 the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors announced that its member journals would require registration of clinical trials in a public registry at or before the start of participant enrolment as a condition of consideration for publication, to counter selective reporting. Nosek and colleagues described pre-registration as a way to distinguish confirmatory from exploratory research and to reduce bias from analytic flexibility.
text.ur: 2004 mein International Committee of Medical Journal Editors ne elaan kiya ke is ke member journals shaya karne par ghaur ki shart ke taur par shirkat karne walon ki bharti ke aaghaz par ya pehle clinical trials ki public registry mein registration lazmi karenge, chun-chun kar report karne ka tor karne ke liye. Nosek aur saathiyon ne pre-registration ko tasdeeqi ko tajrabaati research se alag karne aur tajziye ki lachak se bias kam karne ka tareeqa bayan kiya.

text.en: **Before, Specific, Public, Label.** Register before recruiting, be specific, keep it public and label exploratory work.
text.ur: **Pehle, Khaas, Public, Label.** Bharti se pehle register karein, khaas hon, public rakhein aur tajrabaati kaam ko label karein.

summary.en: Register trials publicly before the first participant, with a specific primary outcome and analysis plan.
summary.ur: Pehle shirkat karne wale se pehle trials public taur par register karein, khaas primary outcome aur analysis plan ke saath.

summary.en: Outcome switching and selective reporting are what registration is designed to expose.
summary.ur: Outcome switching aur chun-chun kar report karna wohi hain jinhein registration benaqab karne ke liye bani hai.

summary.en: Share data and materials openly when ethical, and always protect participants' privacy.
summary.ur: Jahan akhlaqi ho data aur materials khulle taur par share karein, aur shirkat karne walon ki nijiyat hamesha mehfooz rakhein.
